Subject: Deployment mode qualification — shared vs dedicated (follow-up)

Hi Emma / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we heard from FinPay:
- Peak payroll windows (2x daily spikes) drive high QPS for inference endpoints; you saw latency spikes that correlate with other tenant activity on shared infra ("noisy neighbor").
- Primary goals are predictable throughput during peaks, tight tail-latency, and clear isolation for regulated workloads.
- Compliance note: SOC2 + customer data residency are important for some of your customers.

Redwood options we reviewed (high level):
- Hosted API — fastest to adopt (simple API keys, no infra to manage). Good fit for dev/test and low-to-medium predictability workloads. Soft isolation; we use workload prioritization but not reserved GPUs.
- Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools for your account, configurable autoscale policies and burst capacity, and stronger isolation boundaries (no shared-tenancy on the same GPUs). This is where we can offer predictable throughput and tighter SLO commitments.
- Private (VPC / on-prem) — for strict compliance/regulatory needs: private control plane, customer-managed networking, optional on-prem package and KMS/HSM integration.

Open asks / next steps from Redwood:
1) Can you share a short traffic profile (typical qps, peak qps, average sequence length, and % of requests during peak windows)? This will help sizing for Dedicated.
2) What are your SLO targets for latency (p95 / p99) and acceptable error/availability targets?
3) Which teams should join the technical deep-dive? (Infra / App owners / Security)

I attached the mutual action plan (MAP) and a short pricing overview for Dedicated so you have the numbers we discussed.

Proposed follow-up: technical deep-dive to walk through isolation, eviction/backpressure behavior, and SLA options — Tue, Apr 13 at 11:00 AM PT. Does that work?

Thanks — I can sync Marissa and Vivek from infra on our side for the deep-dive.

Best,

Hi Emma / Tom —

Thanks — quick answers to your questions ahead of Tuesday's deep-dive: 

Noisy neighbor / isolation details (short):
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools mean your workloads run on capacity that is not shared at the GPU level with other tenants. That eliminates noisy-neighbor interference caused by co-located inference or batch jobs on the same GPU. We also provide tenant-level cgroups and scheduler pinning to reduce cross-VM interference for any multi-tenant host-level services.
- Hosted API: multi-tenant scheduling with priority lanes; good for predictability at low scale but not a substitute for physical isolation. We can tune rate limits and priority, but there is still a residual risk of tail-latency spikes during noisy events.
- Private VPC / on-prem: complete control — you own the infra or we deploy in your VPC with strict network/isolation controls and optional HSM/KMS for keys.

SLA / SLO guidance:
- Typical Dedicated guidance (default configs): p95 request latency targets for short text-generation workloads in the 150–300ms range; p99 typically under 1s for standard prompt sizes. For larger payloads or multi-turn chat with long sequences these numbers shift — we'll size based on your seq length and token mix.
- For Dedicated and Private we offer contractual SLAs (uptime + latency commitment tiers) as part of a reserved capacity agreement. Hosted customers get best-effort SLAs with usage-based credits for major incidents. We'll surface standard SLA language during the legal review.

Attached is a short isolation brief that summarizes how Dedicated enforces boundaries and the operational playbook for noisy neighbor incidents.
